source.title: Generalized AdaGrad (G-AdaGrad) and Adam: A State-Space Perspective

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports optimizer convergence and training-loss experiments, but does not measure train–test generalization gaps or test any listed version of the claim.
record.gate_note: MNIST plots report convergence/optimality gap and training loss for G-AdaGrad and Adam under parameter settings. These are optimizer performance results, not held-out generalization results. Optimizer claims in the introduction that cite prior work are not this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study cites Wilson et al. about adaptive-method underperformance but does not test V4 or any other version. Its own results concern continuous-time optimization convergence, linear-regression optimality gaps, and logistic-regression training loss. Figure 2 displays training and test data with a fitted decision boundary but reports no held-out performance comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. More precisely, the authors propose G-AdaGrad and continuous-time state-space models for G-AdaGrad and Adam, present deterministic convergence proofs under stated assumptions and parameter conditions, and describe MNIST regression experiments as empirical validation.
record.recipe_differences: Continuous-time optimizer models and convergence analysis, with empirical MNIST optimization experiments; no generalization-gap method or measure.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported convergence varies with G-AdaGrad's α and Adam's relative λ1/λ2 values; smaller α converges faster, while a smaller or larger λ1/λ2 leads to oscillations or slower convergence.

fits_no_version.finding: On MNIST-derived linear and logistic regression tasks, smaller tested G-AdaGrad exponents converge faster; changing Adam's moment-parameter ratio can produce oscillations or slower convergence (Section 4; Figures 1 and 3). These are optimization outcomes without held-out optimizer comparisons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: G-AdaGrad and Adam convergence depends on their algorithm parameters.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Conference on Decision and Control
record.problems: The experiments use MNIST-derived binary classification and linear regression, but report optimization convergence and training loss only; no held-out evaluation or uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying rows: experimental outcomes concern convergence/optimality gap and training loss, not the claim's train–test gap or held-out performance.

Figure 2's test-data visualization means the record should avoid implying that test data never appear; it supplies no result testing these versions.
